pending_queue.what: Draft content and queued changes require administrator approval. Independent supported edits can survive separate Apply requests only through complete approved snapshot history. The content fingerprint ignores exactly the WordPress runtime job flags _pingme, _encloseme and _trackbackme; content, SEO, author, permalink, taxonomy and other plugin metadata remain protected. gsc_warehouse.what: Local SQLite archive of retrieved GSC observations. Local retention avoids server pruning, but upstream sampling, API limits and missing dates still constrain coverage.

outcome_engine.what: Compare observed clicks and leads around applied edits with a site comparison. Results are observational; confounding and overlapping interventions can remain.

rank_math_schema.what: Edit Rank Math Schema Builder rows in place by dot path (offers.price etc). The ONLY path to those capitalised postmeta arrays — draft_update_postmeta lowercases the key and flattens the array. %variable% placeholders survive.

stack_introspection.what: Read installed plugins, captured admin menus and redacted settings. Inspect runtime schemas and registered adapter controls before a feature plan; discovery is explicitly incomplete where no adapter is available.

asset_references.what: Find and swap a media URL WHEREVER it is stored — post_content of any post type, postmeta, options, termmeta — searching every spelling (JSON-escaped, protocol-relative, root-relative, http twin). This is the way into plugins that keep content outside post_content and have no dedicated tool: popup overlays, sliders, theme option backgrounds. Serialized values are unserialized/rewritten/re-serialized so length prefixes stay valid; rows holding non-stdClass objects are refused, not risked. media_audit finds the heavy files worth swapping.

render_health_guard.what: Does the page still WORK after a change? Queue captures a rendered-page baseline (empty-state strings, markup-anchored element counts, shortcode leakage, PHP errors, HTTP status); the post-apply audit re-fetches cache-busted and compares. A builder empty-state appearing or an element population vanishing is flagged CRITICAL on the pending row + activity log + dashboard within ~30s of apply. Reports only; never auto-reverts. Companion lint change: failures are split into introduced-by-this-change vs pre_existing-in-current-body, and pre-existing structural failures no longer hard-block unrelated edits.
render_health_guard.tools: (automatic on queue + apply; see lint introduced/pre_existing in queue responses)

setting_writes.what: Read current plugin capability/schema evidence, preview a typed scalar setting change, then use the existing review flow. Unsupported values or inactive controls remain explicit; a stored value does not verify its visible effect.

bulk_term_tagging.what: Assign ONE taxonomy term to MANY posts in a single approval. Solves the two ways wp-admin gets this wrong: its category filter misses products sitting in deeper sub-terms, and its product search matches DESCRIPTIONS so accessories that merely mention a brand get tagged. Matching is title_contains (SQL LIKE on post_title only), in_term (a term AND all its children), or explicit post_ids. Returns a plan with matched / already-tagged / will-change counts before anything is queued; rollback restores the exact prior terms on every post, including posts that had none. Products are eligible here even though they are off-limits to body edits, because term relationships cannot corrupt product content or pricing.

content_strategy.what: Claude discovers and maintains niche scope from existing sources and notes. New content does not need an existing GSC gap.

content_workflow.what: Prepare a source-backed workflow, execute it with the connected agent, then verify actual result IDs. A saved plan is not proof of created or applied content.

content_research.what: Bounded competitor observations and claim candidates with extraction limits; no factual or global-originality certification.

prospective_research.what: Research a source-anchored new topic before an article exists, compare observed excerpts and primary sources, and inspect existing content without requiring GSC gaps. Proposed value remains explicitly unverified.

memory_consistency.what: whoami/get_site_memory flag potentially outdated durable guidance for review. Strategy freshness ignores routine Sessions logs while preserving Rules, Decisions and unstructured legacy notes.

public_content_author.what: Explicit existing author or validated saved default for new posts/pages; no automation-login fallback.

external_provider_records.what: Dated, scoped, actor-bound Ubersuggest observations with explicit transcription provenance and uncertainty.

native_frontend_settings.what: Reviewed SiteGround native frontend toggles, queued apply and conflict-aware rollback.

brain_concurrency.what: Shared-brain writes require expected fingerprint and database lock. Old bridge writers must update.

- - **Before changing homepage/service-page SEO titles, pull three data points first.** Never reorder a title based on intuition or GSC-CTR-curves alone.

1. **Service-page architecture:** does a dedicated page exist for the term you're considering leading with? If yes, the homepage should de-tune from it. If no, the homepage IS the de-facto landing page and should keep that term prominent. (Example: no /med-spa/ page exists; aesthetic-treatments-irving-tx covers botox/microneedling but isn't named "med spa" — so the homepage is the only page that can rank for "med spa irving.")
2. **Current GSC rank position on the term you're moving:** if we already rank page 1 for it, moving it out of title-position-1 risks a relevance-signal downgrade that costs the ranking. Check with gsc_page_queries before re-ordering.
3. **Compare ALL realistic opportunities on the page, not just CTR-gap signals.** A 352-imp query at pos 6.5 with 0 CTR (e.g. "irving health center") may dwarf a brand-CTR-gap rescue. List page-1 zero-CTR queries first, then brand-CTR underperformance second.

**Why:** 2026-05-12 — Recommended brand-first homepage title based on brand-CTR-gap (8.3% vs 18.7% expected). User pushed back: "med spa has more search volume." Pulled data: live title already led with "Med Spa" and ranked pos 9 for "med spa irving" — brand-first would demote that signal and likely cost the ranking. User was right; I was optimizing the smaller pond.
- - **Site niche (strict scope — Google penalizes off-topic content):** med spa / aesthetic treatments (botox, fillers, microneedling, laser, IPL, chemical peels), IV therapy / IV hydration, medical weight loss (GLP-1, semaglutide, tirzepatide, Wegovy, Ozempic, Mounjaro, Zepbound, B12/Lipo-B injections), hormone optimization (HRT, TRT, bioidentical, menopause, andropause, peptides), wellness coaching, longevity / preventive care, metabolic health (insulin resistance, A1C, lab-driven plans). 6. **Updated research (recency)**: 2025-2026 findings, post-FDA-update protocols, new compounding rules. Recency by itself is a thin signal but combined with synthesis or local context becomes strong.

**The audit question to ask BEFORE finishing any service-page optimization:** *"What's on this page that isn't already on the top 5 pages in the SERP?"* If the answer is "nothing", the page may rank but it won't index well. - ## Paragraph breaks follow MEANING, not sentence counts (REVISES the older "2-3 sentence max" rule)

The earlier "2-3 sentences max per paragraph" guidance was a crude band-aid for wall-of-text paste-ins from Google Docs. It is NOT the actual writing principle. From 2026-05-13 forward use the meaning-based rule below for every new post/page AND every optimization of an existing post/page:

- **Break the paragraph when**: the idea shifts, the argument pivots, the path or direction of the prose changes, you want a sentence to be remembered (emphasis), or you set up a contrast that needs to land.
- **Stay together when**: every sentence develops the same point and breaking would lose the thread. Forcing a break mid-argument creates choppy, robotic prose.
- **Single-sentence paragraphs are GREAT** when the sentence carries weight on its own. Example: *"Real drowning is silent."* deserves its own line. *"We also have on-site CT."* does not. Use single-sentence paragraphs for punchlines, pivots, contrasts, or memorability anchors that the reader should walk away with.
- **4-5 sentence paragraphs are FINE** when every sentence develops the same point and they truly need each other. A coherent argument step does not need to be artificially broken.
- The standard is flow + emphasis + meaning, not sentence count. NYT, The Atlantic, and patient-facing NEJM material all follow this. So do we.

This applies to every word the cc-assistant tool writes or edits on this site: new blog posts, new pages, optimization of existing posts, optimization of existing pages, and meta/title/description copy.
